title: [planner].account pins the Planner account: Pool.pick("planner") returns it, `orchestrator pick planner` prints it (with a stderr notice when it is cooling or over budget), and the restart instruction no longer says to switch accounts
spec:
Goal T-1481 (human 2026-10-01: stay on one account the whole time). Facts (main 355583c): Pool.pick(role, avoid=None) in orchestrator/pool.py (~459-477) is least-loaded-with-headroom over self.accounts (planner ceiling 1.0, skips cooling and over-daily-budget accounts, returns None when nothing has headroom). cli.py `pick` (~581-600) calls pl.tally_planner(), then pl.pick(a.role), exits 3 with "hold: no account with headroom" on None, prints "<id>\t<config_dir>", and with --model prints the model line. planner_runs.py calls pool.pick("planner") at ~457 (run) and ~1285 (run_group) for headless launches. CLAUDE.md line 22 and .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md line 18 (rule 9) say: "restart the session on the account `orchestrator pick planner` names". README.md line 43 documents `orchestrator pick`. The [planner] table in pool.toml has no account key today; an unknown key is ignored.

Change:
1. pool.py: Pool.pick(role, avoid=None): when role == "planner" and self.cfg.get("planner", {}).get("account") names an id in self.accounts, return that account unconditionally (cooling, utilization and daily budget do not matter: the human wants one account, and holding the Planner would stop everything). An unknown or missing id falls through to today's least-loaded selection unchanged. Other roles are unchanged. Add the rule to the docstring.
2. cli.py `pick`: after picking, when role == "planner" and the pin applied, and the account is cooling or over its daily budget, print one stderr line `pick: pinned planner account <id> is <cooling for Ns | over daily budget>; continuing on it` and still print the account line and exit 0. Expose the applied-pin fact without duplicating the rule: e.g. Pool.planner_pin() -> account id | None, used by both pick() and the CLI.
3. Shipped default in pool.toml [planner]: a commented example line `# account = "A"  # pin the Planner (interactive and headless) to one account; unset = least-loaded` directly under handover_context_tokens. Do NOT set a live value in the committed file; the Planner sets the live pin in the checkout.
4. Docs: CLAUDE.md line 22 and .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md line 18 become: `9. At 150k context tokens (or after 150 turns): \`uv run orchestrator handover --reason context\`, then restart the session with \`f orch\` on the same account (\`orchestrator pick planner\` honours [planner].account).` Keep both files byte-identical in that line. README.md line 43: add one sentence that [planner].account pins the Planner account and pick planner then always prints it.

Tests that assert the old behaviour (SPEC RULE): tests/test_pool.py ~74 asserts pick("planner").id == "A" with no pin (least-loaded), and tests/test_cli.py 663-712 (pick prints account + config dir, --model line) run without a pin: all must pass unchanged. Add the new tests next to them using the same fixtures: set self.p.cfg["planner"] = {"account": "B"} (or the harness's second account id) and assert the pin wins even when that account is cooling or over budget, and that an unknown id falls back to least-loaded.

Rollback: `git revert` of the merge; a live `account` key is then ignored (unknown key). Out of scope: planner_runs.py (it already calls pool.pick, so the pin reaches headless launches without a change), goals.py, the f orch launcher (protected path; it calls `orchestrator pick planner --model`, so it needs no edit).

Work on the task branch cut from goal/T-1481. Commit first, then run the focused tests (tests/test_pool.py, tests/test_cli.py) in the foreground; never background a command and never run the full gate. Write tests as unittest.TestCase methods using tests/_harness.py like the neighbouring tests.
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py::test_pick_planner_honours_pinned_account: passes: with cfg['planner']['account'] = <second account id>, Pool.pick('planner') returns that account while it has the higher utilization, while it is cooling (cooldown_until in the future) and while day_tokens + planner_day_tokens >= daily_budget; with an unknown id or no key, pick('planner') returns the least-loaded account exactly as before; pick('scout') ignores the pin

tests/test_cli.py::test_pick_planner_prints_pinned_account_with_notice: passes: `orchestrator pick planner` with a pinned, cooling account prints `<id>\t<config_dir>` on stdout, exits 0, and prints one stderr line containing 'pinned planner account' and the id; without a pin the existing pick tests pass unchanged

CLAUDE.md and .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md rule 9 both read 'restart the session with `f orch` on the same account' and no longer contain 'on the account `orchestrator pick planner` names'; `grep -c 'orchestrator pick planner. names' CLAUDE.md .orchestrator/prompts/planner.md` prints 0 for both
